searchText: Do any clients have a "verify DB" option? Would be nice if I could "download" a copy of a client's DB from strangers on the internet and then verify it afterwards. E.g., walk the block history and verify block hashes, then verify the state tried matches the state root at the end. I could then get a copy of of the DB off of S3 or glacier or something, verify it, then start my node for the first time. That sounds a lot like warp sync. The challenge is keeping the remote database up to date (and avoiding griefing attacks where you wind up downloading gigabytes of database only to discover it's invalid) The idea would be to acquire the DB from a semi-trusted source. E.g., buy it from a company that sells copies of the DB (and high bandwidth download options) or something. Specifically useful for syncing in the cloud, e.g., buy access to an image that is maintained by a for profit entity. <@!301186049323958275> I think it would suffice to ensure that the stateroot for block X in that db is in fact the stateroot for the canon chain at that height If the db has been modified, it will fail when resolving the hashes in the trie Oh wait. Maybe it won't on _read_ <jadler> Question: are both branches of conditionals jumpdests, or only one of them? you mean the JUMPI instruction? <jadler> Yeah, I guess only the destination needs to be JUMPDEST. Because if there is no jump, then the execution simply continues to the next instruction after JUMPI <jadler> That's what I thought <jadler> In that case, if the jump is taken, the non-taken code would still need to be in the witness, if code is chunked using jumpdests. <jadler> If you use MAST then you don't have this issue <alexberegszaszi> What is MAST? correct. But that is only if the code is chunked by jumpdests 🙂 MAST is Merklelised Abstract Syntax Tree? I think it is used on TapRoot, bitcoin sub-project <alexberegszaszi> perhaps the better term is "chunked by basic blocks" ? (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <Alexey> correct. But that is only if the code is chunked by jumpdests 🙂) <jadler> 👆 (re @alexberegszaszi: perhaps the better term is "chunked by basic blocks" ?) <jadler> It would be interesting to see the difference in size of witnesses between the two chunking schemes (only jumpdests or basic blocks). <alexberegszaszi> Ah ok, MAST was an intuition with the early ewasm work. I just can't find the original post on it. It was never implemented though. (Going back to 2016.) (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <Alexey> MAST is Merklelised Abstract Syntax Tree?)
